interactions.explanation: Both are potent actives that can destabilize each other and increase irritation when applied together; best used at different times of day.
Benzoyl peroxide can oxidize and deactivate retinol, and combined use significantly increases risk of dryness and irritation.
Layering multiple exfoliating acids increases the risk of over-exfoliation and barrier damage.
Older concerns about incompatibility are largely unsubstantiated at typical cosmetic concentrations; generally safe to combine.
Combining retinol with alpha hydroxy acids can compound irritation and dryness; alternate nights are recommended.
Hyaluronic acid helps offset the dryness commonly caused by retinol use.

hazards.note: Restricted or prohibited concentration in some regions; requires professional guidance for prolonged use.
Common source of contact sensitization, especially for sensitive or compromised skin barriers.
